title: Chemistry — The periodic table
welcome_lead: Today's adventure: Chemistry — The periodic table — combined-science-trilogy-8464-derived, section 4.1.2.
meta_desc: GCSE Combined Science (AQA) practice covering Chemistry — The periodic table, specification section 4.1.2.
final_note: You worked through Chemistry — The periodic table — 36 specification statements.

concepts.def: The arrangement of all the elements in order of atomic (proton) number, set out so that elements with similar properties fall in the same column.
A column of the periodic table. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons and so have similar chemical properties.
A row of the periodic table. The period number equals the number of occupied electron shells in an atom of the element.
The number of protons in the nucleus of an atom. It fixes the element's place in the periodic table.
The electrons in the highest occupied shell of an atom. Their number decides the group and controls the element's chemical reactions.
The repeating of similar properties at regular intervals along the order of elements, which is why the table is called periodic.
The mass measure used to order elements before subatomic particles were known; now called relative atomic mass.
Spaces left in his table for elements he believed had not yet been discovered, with properties predicted from the neighbouring elements.
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, which is why atomic weight does not always rise with proton number.
An element that reacts to form positive ions. Metals lie to the left and towards the bottom of the periodic table.
An element that does not form positive ions. Non-metals lie towards the right and top of the periodic table.
An ion formed when an atom loses one or more electrons, leaving more protons than electrons.
The elements of Group 0. They are unreactive and do not easily form molecules because their atoms have stable electron arrangements.
An outer shell holding eight electrons, or two in the case of helium, so the atom has no tendency to gain, lose or share electrons.
Boiling points increase with increasing relative atomic mass, that is, going down the group.
The elements of Group 1. Their characteristic properties follow from the single electron in the outer shell of their atoms.
The alkaline compound produced, along with hydrogen, when a Group 1 metal reacts with water.
Reactivity increases going down the group, as the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more easily lost.
The elements of Group 7. They are non-metals with seven outer electrons whose atoms go about in pairs as molecules.
A molecule made of two atoms joined together, the form in which the halogen elements exist, such as Cl2 and Br2.
The ionic compound formed when a halogen reacts with a metal, such as sodium chloride or iron bromide.
The covalent compound formed when a halogen reacts with a non-metal, such as hydrogen chloride.
Reactivity decreases going down the group, as the outer shell is further from the nucleus and an electron is gained less easily.
A reaction in which a more reactive halogen takes the place of a less reactive halogen in an aqueous solution of its salt.

mcqs.q: In the modern periodic table the elements are set out one after another in order of which quantity?
options: Atomic (proton) number, going up by one at each step
Relative atomic mass, the larger number in each box
The number of occupied electron shells it has
Number of neutrons in the nucleus of an atom
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the elements are arranged in order of atomic (proton) number, and that number climbs by one at every step.

mcqs.q: Why is the table of the elements described as periodic?
options: Because the table is revised at regular periods as new elements appear
Because elements with similar properties recur at regular intervals
Because every row repeats the properties of the row above it
Because each element repeats the electron count before it
mcqs.explain: The specification says the table is called periodic because similar properties occur at regular intervals along it.

mcqs.q: Chlorine and bromine are both in Group 7 and react in similar ways. What do atoms of these two elements share?
options: The same total number of electrons in the whole atom
The same number of occupied shells in the atom
The same number of outer electrons in an atom
The same number of neutrons in the nucleus
mcqs.explain: Elements in one group have the same number of outer electrons, and that is what gives them similar chemical properties.

mcqs.q: An atom of element X has the electronic structure 2,8,7. Where in the periodic table is X found?
options: Group 3 and Period 7, reading its three occupied shells
Group 17 and Period 3, counting all the electrons
Group 7 and Period 7, both read from the outer shell
Group 7 and Period 3, from seven outer electrons
mcqs.explain: Seven electrons in the outer shell places X in Group 7, and three occupied shells places it in Period 3.

mcqs.q: Rubidium lies below potassium in Group 1. From its position, what can be predicted about its reaction with water?
options: It reacts less vigorously than potassium, being a heavier metal
It reacts more vigorously than potassium, giving off hydrogen gas
It reacts to give rubidium oxide along with hydrogen gas
It reacts much like strontium, its neighbour in that period
mcqs.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1, so rubidium reacts more vigorously than potassium and gives rubidium hydroxide and hydrogen.

mcqs.q: Before protons, neutrons and electrons were discovered, how did scientists attempt to classify the elements?
options: By arranging them in order of the atomic number
By arranging them in order of their outer electron counts
By arranging them in order of their atomic weights
By arranging them in order of their neutron count
mcqs.explain: The specification states that before those particles were known, scientists classified elements by ordering them by atomic weight.

mcqs.q: What problem arose in the early periodic tables when the strict order of atomic weights was followed?
options: Faulty weight values scattered elements far from their true partners
The atomic weights themselves had all been measured wrongly
Permanent gaps appeared that no element could ever fill
Some elements were placed in groups they did not belong in
mcqs.explain: The specification states that early tables were incomplete and that strict weight order put some elements in inappropriate groups.

mcqs.q: Mendeleev left gaps in his periodic table. Why did he do this?
options: He expected undiscovered elements to fill them
He believed that no element could ever exist there
He thought those places in nature were forever empty
He was unsure of several measured atomic weights
mcqs.explain: Mendeleev overcame some of the problems by leaving gaps for elements he thought had not yet been discovered.

mcqs.q: Knowledge of isotopes helped chemists understand the periodic table. What exactly did it explain?
options: Why atomic weights could be measured far more precisely
Why two atoms of one element hold different protons
Why an order based on atomic weights is not always correct
Why Mendeleev's swapped pairs were mistakes after all
mcqs.explain: Isotope mixtures mean atomic weight does not always rise with proton number, which explains the pairs Mendeleev had to swap.

mcqs.q: Sodium reacts to form Na+ ions and sulfur does not form positive ions. What does this tell you about them?
options: Sodium is a non-metal and sulfur is a metal
Both are metals, as each takes part in reactions
Both are non-metals, since neither formed a negative ion
Sodium is a metal and sulfur is a non-metal element
mcqs.explain: Elements that react to form positive ions are metals; elements that do not form positive ions are non-metals.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly describes where metals and non-metals sit in the periodic table?
options: Most elements are metals, on the left and lower down
Most elements are metals, on the right near the top
Most elements are non-metals, on the left and lower down
Most elements are non-metals, over on the right
mcqs.explain: The majority of elements are metals, found to the left and towards the bottom, with non-metals towards the right and top.

mcqs.q: Which pair of properties would you expect a typical metal to show, in contrast to a typical non-metal?
options: A poor conductor of heat that forms negative ions
A good heat conductor that forms positive ions
A good conductor of heat, yet it forms negative ions
A poor conductor of heat which forms positive ions
mcqs.explain: Metals conduct heat and electricity well and react to form positive ions; typical non-metals do neither.

mcqs.q: Magnesium has the electronic structure 2,8,2. How does this relate to its position in the periodic table?
options: Two outer electrons put it in Group 2, on the right
Ten inner electrons put it in Group 10 instead
Two outer electrons make it a non-metal in Group 2
Two outer electrons put it in Group 2, among the metals
mcqs.explain: Two outer electrons place magnesium in Group 2, on the left of the table, where elements lose electrons to form positive ions.

mcqs.q: Why does magnesium react to form Mg2+ ions while chlorine reacts to form Cl- ions?
options: Magnesium loses its two outer electrons; chlorine gains one
Magnesium gains six electrons and chlorine loses seven
Magnesium has more protons than chlorine has in total
Magnesium has outer electrons it readily gives away
mcqs.explain: Reactions follow the arrangement of electrons: an atom with few outer electrons loses them, one with a nearly full shell gains.

mcqs.q: The noble gases in Group 0 are unreactive. Which statement explains this and describes their outer shells?
options: Their outer shells are empty, so there is nothing left to react
Their arrangements are stable, eight outer but two in helium
Every one of them holds exactly eight electrons in the outer shell
They travel as pairs, so their bonds are already used
mcqs.explain: Noble gases are unreactive because their atoms have stable electron arrangements: eight outer electrons, or two in helium.

mcqs.q: Argon has the electronic structure 2,8,8. Why does argon not easily form molecules?
options: It has already shared its electrons within a pair
Its atoms already exist joined together in pairs
Its outer shell is stable, so it need not share
Its outer shell has no electrons available to share
mcqs.explain: With a stable outer arrangement, argon has no tendency to gain, lose or share electrons, so it does not easily form molecules.

mcqs.q: What happens to the boiling points of the noble gases as relative atomic mass increases down Group 0?
options: They increase steadily going further down the group
They decrease as the gases become lighter down it
They stay the same, as these gases are stable
They fall sharply, halving with each step down
mcqs.explain: The specification states that the boiling points of the noble gases increase with increasing relative atomic mass.

mcqs.q: Boiling points in Group 0 are helium -269 C, neon -246 C, argon -186 C. Predict the boiling point of krypton.
options: Below -269 C, continuing past helium at the top
About -153 C, carrying the rise further down
About -230 C, falling below argon down the group
About -246 C, the same value as neon shows
mcqs.explain: Boiling points increase down Group 0, so krypton, below argon, must boil at a higher temperature than -186 C.

mcqs.q: The Group 1 elements are known as the alkali metals. Which feature of their atoms gives them their characteristic properties?
options: Their atoms each hold just a single occupied electron shell
Their atoms each need a single electron more to fill a shell
Their atoms each have a single electron in the outer shell
Their atoms each have a single proton in the nucleus
mcqs.explain: Group 1 elements have characteristic properties because of the single electron in their outer shell.

mcqs.q: A small piece of potassium is dropped onto water. What are the products of the reaction?
options: Potassium oxide and hydrogen gas are both formed
Potassium chloride and hydrogen gas are given off
Potassium oxide and oxygen gas are given off
Potassium hydroxide and hydrogen gas form
mcqs.explain: A Group 1 metal reacts with water to give a metal hydroxide and hydrogen: 2K + 2H2O gives 2KOH + H2.

mcqs.q: Lithium is burned in oxygen, and separately sodium is burned in chlorine. What are the two products?
options: Lithium oxide and covalent sodium chloride molecules
Lithium oxide, Li2O, and sodium chloride, NaCl, are made
Lithium hydroxide and sodium chloride solution
Lithium oxide, LiO, plus sodium chloride, NaCl2
mcqs.explain: Group 1 metals burn in oxygen to give the metal oxide and in chlorine to give the metal chloride: 4Li + O2 gives 2Li2O.

mcqs.q: Lithium reacts steadily with water, sodium melts into a ball and potassium bursts into flame. Predict how caesium behaves.
options: Less vigorously than lithium, being the heaviest metal here
About the same as potassium, as both are in Group 1
Even more vigorously than potassium, reacting explosively
Steadily, because its outer electron is held tightly
mcqs.explain: Reactivity increases down Group 1, so caesium, well below potassium, reacts more violently still.

mcqs.q: Why does the reactivity of the Group 1 metals increase going down the group?
options: Atoms lower down have many more electrons to give away
Atoms lower down have more protons pulling on the shell
Atoms lower down need to gain fewer electrons
The outer electron is further out, so easily lost
mcqs.explain: Going down the group the outer electron is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so the attraction is weaker and it is lost more easily.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly describes the elements of Group 7, the halogens?
options: Non-metals with seven outer electrons, found as pairs
Non-metals with seven outer electrons, existing as atoms
Metals with seven outer electrons, going about in pairs
Non-metals with seven electron shells, joined in pairs
mcqs.explain: The halogens are non-metals with seven electrons in the outer shell, and they consist of molecules made of pairs of atoms.

mcqs.q: Chlorine reacts with sodium, and separately with hydrogen. What kinds of compound are formed?
options: An ionic compound with sodium, and ions with hydrogen too
A covalent compound with sodium, and ions with hydrogen
An ionic compound with sodium, and a molecule with hydrogen
A covalent compound in both, since chlorine is a non-metal
mcqs.explain: A halogen with a metal gives an ionic metal halide, NaCl; with a non-metal it gives a covalent molecule, HCl.

mcqs.q: Melting points in Group 7 are chlorine -101 C, bromine -7 C, iodine 114 C. Predict the melting point of astatine.
options: About -150 C, since reactivity falls down the group
About -90 C, dropping since reactivity falls
About 114 C, matching iodine in the group
About 300 C, continuing the rise on below iodine
mcqs.explain: Melting and boiling points increase down Group 7 as relative molecular mass increases, so astatine melts above iodine.

mcqs.q: Why does the reactivity of the halogens decrease going down Group 7?
options: The outer shell is further out, so gaining one is harder
Larger atoms are heavier, so they must react more sluggishly
Extra shells lower down leave fewer outer electrons exposed
Atoms lower down lose their outer electrons more easily
mcqs.explain: Going down the group the outer shell is further from the nucleus and more shielded, so an electron is attracted and gained less easily.

mcqs.q: Chlorine solution is added to colourless potassium bromide solution. What is observed, and why?
options: No change, as bromine is the more reactive halogen
It turns orange, as bromine has been displaced
It turns orange as bromine displaces the chlorine
No change, since both elements sit in the same group
mcqs.explain: Chlorine is more reactive than bromine, so it displaces bromine from the solution of its salt: Cl2 + 2KBr gives 2KCl + Br2.

mcqs.q: An atom of element Z has 15 protons. Where in the periodic table is Z found?
options: Group 5 and Period 3, from five outer electrons
Group 3 and Period 5, counting its three shells
Group 15 and Period 3, adding all its electrons
Group 5 and Period 5, both from the outer shell
mcqs.explain: 15 protons means 15 electrons, arranged 2,8,5. Five outer electrons give Group 5 and three occupied shells give Period 3.

mcqs.q: An atom of element Q has 19 protons. What does an atom of Q do when it reacts?
options: Loses one electron to form a 1+ ion
Loses its outer electron, giving a 1- ion
Gains seven electrons to form a 7- ion
Loses four electrons to make a 4+ ion
mcqs.explain: 19 protons means 19 electrons, arranged 2,8,8,1. The single outer electron is lost, so Q is a metal forming a 1+ ion.
